title: Quantification of ecological complexity and resilience from multivariate biological metrics datasets using singular value decomposition entropy
author: Ginebreda, Sabater-Liesa, et al.

steps.title: Collect biological monitoring data
steps.instruction: Gather measurements of six phytoplankton‑related variables—Shannon‑Wiener diversity, number of species, cell density, biovolume, chlorophyll‑a concentration, and alkaline phosphatase activity (APA)—from twelve sampling sites (six upstream of the Mequinenza, Riba‑roja and Flix reservoirs and six downstream) across multiple monitoring campaigns.

steps.title: Organize data into matrices
steps.instruction: For each variable, build two rectangular data matrices (A_up and A_down) with rows equal to the number of monitoring campaigns (n) and columns equal to the number of spatial sites (m = 6 for upstream or downstream). Format the matrices as numeric arrays suitable for singular value decomposition.

steps.title: Perform singular value decomposition
steps.instruction: Apply singular value decomposition to each matrix (A_up and A_down) to obtain the set of singular values {λ_A}. Use any standard linear‑algebra library (e.g., NumPy, MATLAB) that returns singular values in descending order.

steps.title: Calculate SVD entropy
steps.instruction: Compute the SVD entropy H(A) for each matrix using Eq. (4): H(A) = ‑∑ p_i log p_i where p_i = λ_i / Σλ_i. Record H_up and H_down for every variable. Expected entropy values lie between 0.38 and 0.72 (38 %–72 % of the maximum).

steps.title: Quantify resilience
steps.instruction: For each variable, calculate the resilience index as 1 – |ΔH| where ΔH = H_up – H_down (Eq. (6)). The resulting resilience values should fall between 0.75 and 0.97 (e.g., APA 0.751, diversity 0.967).

steps.title: Interpret results
steps.instruction: Compare upstream and downstream entropy values; higher upstream entropy indicates greater complexity under natural flow. Resilience values close to 1 suggest the system can maintain its complexity after the reservoir perturbation.
